paragraphs.text: “Joshua,” meaning “Jehovah Is Salvation.” Lit., “Jehoshua,” M; Sy, “Jeshua”; LXXVg, “Jesus.” See Heb 4:8 ftn, “Joshua.”
Or, “chief.” Lit., “great,” MLXXVg.
“Jehovah of armies.” Heb., Yehwahʹ tseva·ʼohthʹ; Gr., Kyʹri·os pan·to·kraʹtor, “Jehovah Almighty”; Luther (German, 1964 ed.), der HERR Zeʹba·oth. This expression occurs 14 times in Haggai’s prophecy.
Or, “the mountainous region.”
Or, “the land.” Heb., ha·ʼaʹrets.
Or, “mankind.” Heb., ha·ʼa·dhamʹ.
Lit., “the great priest.”
“Their God.” Heb., ʼElo·heh·hemʹ.
Or, “angel of.” Heb., mal·ʼakhʹ; Gr., agʹge·los; Lat., nunʹti·us, “messenger.”
“Spirit of.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tum.
“People of the land.” Heb., ʽam ha·ʼaʹrets. Later used contemptuously. Compare Joh 7:47-49.
Lit., “word.”
Lit., “cut.”
Lit., “And I will shake all the nations.”
“Desirable things,” by a change of vowel pointing; M, “desirable (precious) thing,” sing. but evidently in a collective sense, for this word is accompanied by a pl. verb.
Or, “and they, the desirable things of all the nations, must come in.”
“A man.” Heb., ʼish.
Lit., “a soul,” that is, a dead soul. Heb., neʹphesh; Gr., psy·kheiʹ; Lat., aʹni·ma. See Le 21:11 and Nu 6:6 ftns; App 4A.
“In the temple of.” Heb., beheh·khalʹ; Gr., na·oiʹ; Lat., temʹplo. See Mt 23:16 ftn.
Or, “storeroom.”
